question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of the Ka Pomblang Nongkrem festival of the Khasis of Meghalaya?
option_1: A mourning ceremony held for the departed members of a clan
option_2: A ritual performed to seek victory before going to war
option_3: A trading fair at which livestock is exchanged between villages
option_4: A thanksgiving to the deity for a good harvest and a prayer for the prosperity of the people
solution_text:
The correct answer is A thanksgiving to the deity for a good harvest and a prayer for the prosperity of the people.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ka Pomblang Nongkrem, popularly called the Nongkrem dance, is the great five-day autumn festival of the Khasi people of Meghalaya. Its purpose is to offer thanksgiving for a good harvest and to pray for the peace and prosperity of the people. (का पोमब्लांग नोंगक्रेम — खासी जनजाति का धन्यवाद उत्सव)

 

• It is held at Smit, the capital of the Khyrim Syiemship, near Shillong. The central rite is the Pomblang, the sacrificial offering of goats to the deity Ka Blei Synshar and to the ancestors of the ruling clan.

 

• The ceremony is conducted jointly by the Syiem (the chief, who is the secular head) and the Ka Syiem Sad (the high priestess, who is the spiritual head) — a reflection of the matrilineal character of Khasi society.

 

• Unmarried girls dance in the inner circle in gold and silver ornaments, while men, carrying swords and whisks, dance in the outer circle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Names of festivals often carry their meaning, and examiners test this:

◦ Mim Kut of the Mizos — a festival of the maize harvest; the "Mim" stands for the last harvest, representing survival and love, and it is also observed in memory of the departed

◦ Wangala of the Garos — the hundred drums harvest festival, in honour of Saljong, the sun god

◦ Behdienkhlam of the Jaintias — observed to drive away plague and to seek a good harvest

◦ Chapchar Kut of the Mizos — celebrated after the clearing of forest for jhum cultivation

 

• Meghalaya's three principal tribes — the Khasi, Garo and Jaintia — all follow matrilineal descent, in which lineage and property pass through the mother.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Commemoration of the dead is a feature of Mim Kut, not of Nongkrem.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Nongkrem is an agrarian and religious festival, not a martial one.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Livestock fairs such as Pushkar and Sonepur are quite separate from this ritual festival.

question: The Kumbh Mela is held by rotation at how many places in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Four.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kumbh Mela is held by rotation at four places in India: (कुंभ मेला — चार स्थान)

◦ Prayagraj (Allahabad), Uttar Pradesh — at the Triveni Sangam, the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati

◦ Haridwar, Uttarakhand — on the Ganga

◦ Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh — on the Shipra

◦ Nashik-Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra — on the Godavari

 

• A Purna Kumbh is held at each site once in twelve years, so a Kumbh occurs somewhere in India roughly every three years. An Ardh (half) Kumbh is held every six years at Prayagraj and Haridwar, and the Maha Kumbh at Prayagraj after twelve Purna Kumbhs, that is once in 144 years.

 

• The dates are fixed by the positions of the Sun, Moon and Jupiter (Brihaspati) in particular zodiacal signs.

 

• The Kumbh Mela was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2017, and is described as the largest peaceful congregation of pilgrims in the world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kharchi Puja of Tripura is a festival dedicated to the worship of fourteen deities, the family gods of the erstwhile royal house of Tripura, celebrated at the Chaturdasha Temple near Agartala.

 

• Other well-known religious gatherings: the Ambubachi Mela at the Kamakhya temple, Guwahati; the Sonepur Mela in Bihar; and the Magh Mela, the annual observance at Prayagraj in years when no Kumbh falls.

 

NOTE

 

• Two (Option 1) and Three (Option 2) are incorrect; the rotation covers four separate river sites.

 

• Six (Option 4) is incorrect; six years is the interval of the Ardh Kumbh, which is a period, not the number of venues.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Qutb complex in Delhi:

1. The Qutb Minar was begun by Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by Iltutmish.

2. The Alai Darwaza, which forms the southern gateway of the complex, was built by Alauddin Khalji.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2 are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Qutb Minar was begun in about 1199 by Qutbuddin Aibak, founder of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty, who completed only the first storey. It was carried further by his successor Iltutmish, and the upper storeys were later repaired and rebuilt by Firoz Shah Tughlaq. (क़ुतुब मीनार — क़ुतुबुद्दीन ऐबक द्वारा आरंभ, इल्तुतमिश द्वारा पूर्ण)

 

• At about 72.5 metres, it is the tallest brick minaret in the world, built of red sandstone and marble, and was dedicated to the Sufi saint Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki.

 

• Statement 2 is correct. The Alai Darwaza, the southern gateway to the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, was built by Alauddin Khalji in 1311. It is the first building in India to employ the true arch and the true dome in the Islamic manner, and is regarded as a gem of Indo-Islamic architecture.

 

• The complex also contains the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, the earliest extant mosque in Delhi; the Iron Pillar of Chandragupta II, famous for its rust resistance; the Tomb of Iltutmish; and the unfinished Alai Minar. The Qutb Minar and its Monuments were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mughal architecture is known for blending Persian, Islamic, Turkish and Indian styles into a distinctive Indo-Islamic aesthetic, and red sandstone and white marble were its two most commonly used materials.

 

• The earliest Indo-Islamic buildings used the arcuate style — arches and domes — in contrast to the trabeate (post and lintel) style of earlier Indian temples, and employed calligraphy, arabesque and geometric ornament in place of figural sculpture.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the game of volleyball is correct?
option_1: Each team fields seven players on the court at a time
option_2: A team may touch the ball a maximum of three times before returning it over the net
option_3: A player may catch and momentarily hold the ball before passing it
option_4: Every set of a match is won at fifteen points
solution_text:
The correct answer is A team may touch the ball a maximum of three times before returning it over the net.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In volleyball a team is allowed a maximum of three touches to return the ball over the net, conventionally the dig, the set and the spike. A fourth touch is a fault. A block does not count as one of the three touches. (वॉलीबॉल — तीन स्पर्श का नियम)

 

• Each side fields six players on court. After winning the serve, the team rotates clockwise by one position.

 

• A match is played on a best of five sets basis. The first four sets are played to 25 points and the deciding fifth set to 15 points, and a side must always win by a margin of two points (rally point scoring).

 

• The court measures 18 m by 9 m, divided by a net set at 2.43 m for men and 2.24 m for women. A player may not catch, hold or throw the ball; contact must be instantaneous.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The libero is a specialist defensive player who wears a contrasting jersey, may replace any back-row player freely, and may not attack, block or serve.

 

• Volleyball was invented in 1895 by William G. Morgan in the United States, and its world governing body is the Fédération Internationale de Volleyball (FIVB), headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• In basketball, by contrast, each side has five players, a team must attempt a shot within 24 seconds, a player may not remain in the restricted area for more than 3 seconds, and a dribble ends the moment both hands touch the ball simultaneously.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Volleyball is played with six players a side; seven a side is the format of kabaddi and of handball.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Catching or holding the ball is a fault; contact must be momentary.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Only the deciding fifth set is played to 15 points; the others are played to 25.

question: Who was the first Indian to win an individual gold medal at the Paralympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Murlikanta Petkar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Murlikanta Petkar won India's first ever Paralympic gold medal in the 50 m freestyle swimming event at the 1972 Heidelberg Paralympic Games, setting a world record in the process. (मुरलीकांत पेटकर — भारत का पहला पैरालंपिक स्वर्ण)

 

• He was originally a boxer serving in the Indian Army, and was disabled by bullet injuries sustained in the 1965 India-Pakistan war. He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2018, and his life was the basis of the film *Chandu Champion*.

 

• India's other Paralympic gold medallists include Devendra Jhajharia (javelin throw, Athens 2004 and Rio 2016), Mariyappan Thangavelu (high jump, Rio 2016), Avani Lekhara (shooting, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024), Sumit Antil (javelin), Pramod Bhagat and Krishna Nagar (badminton), and Harvinder Singh (archery, Paris 2024).

 

• At the Paris 2024 Paralympics India recorded its best ever performance with 29 medals, including 7 gold. The bronze in the Mixed Team Compound Open archery event was won by Sheetal Devi and Rakesh Kumar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sheetal Devi is the world's first armless female archer to compete internationally, shooting with her feet.

 

• The Paralympic Games are held immediately after the Olympic Games in the same host city, and are governed by the International Paralympic Committee (IPC), headquartered at Bonn, Germany. The first Paralympics were held at Rome in 1960.

 

NOTE

 

• Devendra Jhajharia (Option 1): India's first multiple Paralympic gold medallist, but his first gold came in 2004, long after 1972.

 

• Mariyappan Thangavelu (Option 2): Won high jump gold at Rio 2016.

 

• Avani Lekhara (Option 3): The first Indian woman to win a Paralympic gold, in shooting at Tokyo 2020.

question: The headquarters of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) is located in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manila, Philippines.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Asian Development Bank (ADB) is headquartered at Manila, in the Philippines. It was established in 1966 to promote social and economic development in Asia and the Pacific. (एशियाई विकास बैंk — मनीला, फिलीपींस)

 

• It has 69 members, of which 49 are from the Asia-Pacific region. Japan and the United States are its largest shareholders, holding equal shares; India is among its largest borrowers and a founding member.

 

• ADB provides loans, technical assistance, grants and equity investments, with a stated mission of achieving a prosperous, inclusive, resilient and sustainable Asia and the Pacific, while eradicating extreme poverty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Headquarters of other important international financial institutions:

◦ International Monetary Fund and World Bank — Washington D.C., USA

◦ New Development Bank (BRICS) — Shanghai, China; its Americas Regional Office was announced at São Paulo, Brazil, during the BRICS Foreign Ministers' Meeting of 2018, and its first regional office was at Johannesburg

◦ Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) — Beijing, China, where India is the second largest shareholder

◦ World Trade Organization and UNCTAD — Geneva, Switzerland

◦ Bank for International Settlements — Basel, Switzerland

◦ International Labour Organization — Geneva

 

NOTE

 

• Tokyo (Option 1): Japan is ADB's largest shareholder along with the USA, and the ADB President has traditionally been Japanese, but the Bank's seat is Manila.

 

• Beijing (Option 3): Headquarters of the AIIB, a different multilateral bank founded in 2016.

 

• Singapore (Option 4): A major financial centre, but not the seat of the ADB.

question: Which of the following statements best captures the essence of the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'?
option_1: A memoir of the Revolt of 1857 written by a participant
option_2: A treatise on the theory of Indian classical music
option_3: An economic critique arguing that British rule systematically drained India's wealth
option_4: A collection of poems on rural life in nineteenth-century Bengal
solution_text:
The correct answer is An economic critique arguing that British rule systematically drained India's wealth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) was written by Dadabhai Naoroji, and sets out the celebrated "Drain of Wealth" theory. (गरीबी और भारत में गैर-ब्रिटिश शासन — दादाभाई नौरोजी)

 

• The book argued that a large part of India's wealth was being systematically transferred to Britain through home charges, salaries and pensions of British officials, interest on debt, profits of British capital and one-sided trade — and that this drain was the fundamental cause of India's poverty.

 

• The word "un-British" was deliberate: Naoroji argued that such exploitation was contrary to Britain's own professed liberal principles, appealing to British conscience rather than rejecting British rule outright.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji is known as the "Grand Old Man of India". He was one of the founders of the Indian National Congress, presided over it three times, and in 1892 became the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons, from Central Finsbury on a Liberal Party ticket.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other early economic nationalists and their works: R.C. Dutt, *The Economic History of India*; M.G. Ranade, *Essays on Indian Economics*; and G.V. Joshi. Together they built the economic critique of colonial rule.

 

• Naoroji also produced the first estimates of India's national income and per capita income.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Accounts of 1857 include V.D. Savarkar's *The Indian War of Independence, 1857*.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The classic treatises on Indian music are Bharata's Natyashastra and Sharngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The book is a work of economic analysis, not of poetry.

question: Which of the following statements about a mudflow is correct?
option_1: It is the slowest of all forms of mass movement
option_2: It occurs when a large quantity of water mixes with soil and rock debris, producing a rapid downslope flow
option_3: It involves the free fall of rock fragments from a vertical cliff face
option_4: It occurs only in polar and periglacial regions
solution_text:
The correct answer is It occurs when a large quantity of water mixes with soil and rock debris, producing a rapid downslope flow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A mudflow occurs when a large quantity of water becomes mixed with soil and weathered rock debris, so that the saturated mass behaves like a viscous fluid and moves rapidly downslope, often along a valley or channel. (कीचड़ प्रवाह — जल-संतृप्त मलबे का तीव्र प्रवाह)

 

• Mudflows are typically triggered by heavy rainfall, cloudbursts, the sudden melting of snow or the bursting of a glacial lake, and are especially destructive on deforested slopes and on the loose ash of volcanic terrain, where they are called lahars.

 

• The main types of mass movement, from slowest to fastest, are soil creep, solifluction, earthflow and mudflow, slump, landslide and rockslide, and rockfall.

 

• A rockslide is the sliding of a large mass of rock along a bedding plane or fracture; unlike surface weathering, it affects material to a considerable depth, and it is faster than an earthflow though a rockfall is faster still. A slump is distinguished by the backward rotation of the slipping mass along a curved surface.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mass movement is the downslope movement of material under the direct influence of gravity, without a transporting agent such as running water, wind or ice. Its principal causes are slope steepness, water saturation, earthquakes, deforestation, mining and the undercutting of slopes.

 

• In India, landslides and mudflows are most frequent in the Himalayas and the Western Ghats. The Geological Survey of India is the nodal agency for landslide hazard zonation, and the NDMA issues management guidelines.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The slowest form of mass movement is soil creep, measured in millimetres a year.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The free fall of rock from a cliff is rockfall, the most rapid form.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Solifluction is confined to periglacial regions; mudflows occur widely, particularly in monsoonal and mountainous areas.

question: Which of the following correctly describes Abhinav Bindra's achievement at the 2008 Beijing Olympic Games?
option_1: He won a silver medal in the double trap shooting event
option_2: He won a bronze medal in the 50 m rifle prone event
option_3: He won India's first Olympic gold medal in archery
option_4: He won India's first individual Olympic gold medal, in the 10 m air rifle event
solution_text:
The correct answer is He won India's first individual Olympic gold medal, in the 10 m air rifle event.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abhinav Bindra won the gold medal in the men's 10 m air rifle at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, becoming the first Indian ever to win an individual Olympic gold medal. (अभिनव बिंद्रा — 2008 बीजिंग, व्यक्तिगत ओलंपिक स्वर्ण)

 

• Before this, all of India's Olympic gold medals had come in team hockey. He had earlier won gold at the 2006 ISSF World Championships and at the 2014 Commonwealth Games.

 

• He has been honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (2001), the Padma Bhushan (2009) and the Olympic Order (2024), the highest award of the International Olympic Committee.

 

• At the same Beijing 2008 Games, Sushil Kumar won a bronze in wrestling and Vijender Singh a bronze in boxing, giving India three medals — its best showing at the time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's individual Olympic gold medallists are Abhinav Bindra (shooting, Beijing 2008) and Neeraj Chopra (javelin throw, Tokyo 2020).

 

• Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore won a silver in double trap shooting at the 2004 Athens Olympics, India's first individual Olympic silver.

 

• Neeraj Chopra won the Paris Diamond League 2025 with his opening throw of 88.16 m at the Stade Sébastien Charléty.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The double trap silver was won by Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore at Athens 2004.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Gagan Narang won bronze in the 10 m air rifle at London 2012; Bindra's medal was gold, and in Beijing.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: India has never won an Olympic medal in archery; Harvinder Singh won archery gold at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, a separate event.

question: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) functions under which ministry of the Government of India?
option_2: The Ministry of Science and Technology
option_4: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Ministry of Defence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) functions under the Department of Defence Research and Development of the Ministry of Defence. It was formed in 1958 by amalgamating the Technical Development Establishment, the Directorate of Technical Development and Production, and the Defence Science Organisation. (डीआरडीओ — रक्षा मंत्रालय के अधीन)

 

• Headquartered at DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi, it runs a network of more than fifty laboratories and is India's premier agency for the design and development of defence technology. Its motto is "Balasya Mulam Vigyanam" — the strength of science is the root of power.

 

• Major DRDO products include the Agni and Prithvi missile series, the Akash and Nag missiles, the BrahMos (jointly with Russia), the Tejas Light Combat Aircraft, the Arjun main battle tank, the Rustom and Nishant UAVs, and the Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launcher.

 

• Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, later President of India, headed the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) at DRDO and is known as the "Missile Man of India".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Indian scientific organisations and their parent ministries:

◦ ISRO — Department of Space, which reports directly to the Prime Minister. V. Narayanan took charge as Chairman of ISRO and Secretary, Department of Space, in January 2025, succeeding S. Somanath

◦ CSIR — Ministry of Science and Technology, the largest chain of civilian research laboratories in India

◦ Department of Atomic Energy — also under the Prime Minister

◦ ICAR — Ministry of Agriculture; ICMR — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

 

NOTE

 

• The Ministry of Science and Technology (Option 2): Administers the CSIR, the Department of Science and Technology and the Department of Biotechnology, but not DRDO.

 

• The Ministry of Home Affairs (Option 3): Handles internal security and the central armed police forces.

 

• The Ministry of Electronics and IT (Option 4): Deals with digital governance and the electronics industry.

question:
Which of the following statements about the Bhakra Nangal Project is/are correct?

1. The Bhakra Dam is built on the river Sutlej.

2. It is one of the highest gravity dams in the world.

3. Jawaharlal Nehru described such multipurpose projects as the "temples of modern India".
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3 all are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct. (भाखड़ा नांगल परियोजना)

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Bhakra Dam is built across the river Sutlej at Bhakra in Bilaspur district, Himachal Pradesh, and the Nangal Dam lies downstream in Punjab. The reservoir formed behind it is the Gobind Sagar.

 

• Statement 2 is correct. At about 226 metres, Bhakra is one of the highest gravity dams in the world and the second highest in Asia. A gravity dam resists the thrust of water by its own weight, and is usually built of concrete.

 

• Statement 3 is correct. Jawaharlal Nehru famously called such multipurpose river valley projects the "temples of modern India", seeing in them the union of irrigation, power and industrial development.

 

• The project is a joint undertaking of Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan, managed by the Bhakra Beas Management Board, and it provides irrigation, hydroelectric power and flood control.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major multipurpose projects: the Damodar Valley Corporation, India's first, modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority; Hirakud on the Mahanadi (the longest dam in India); Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna; Sardar Sarovar on the Narmada; Tehri on the Bhagirathi (India's tallest dam); and Rihand on the Son.

 

• A dam need not be a concrete wall; it may equally be an embankment of earth or rock fill. Dams are classified by structure (gravity, arch, buttress, embankment), by purpose (irrigation, power, flood control, multipurpose) and by height. Spillways regulate the release of surplus water, either intermittently or continuously.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them omits one statement that is factually accurate.

question: The Lagrange point L1, where India's Aditya-L1 spacecraft has been placed, lies at approximately what distance from the Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.5 million km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lagrange point L1 of the Sun-Earth system lies about 1.5 million kilometres (15 lakh km) from the Earth in the direction of the Sun — roughly one per cent of the Earth-Sun distance. (एल1 बिंदु — पृथ्वी से लगभग 15 लाख किमी)

 

• A Lagrange point is a position where the gravitational pull of two large bodies balances the centripetal force required for a small object to move with them, so a spacecraft placed there can hold its position with very little fuel. There are five such points, L1 to L5.

 

• The great advantage of L1 is that a satellite there enjoys a continuous, uninterrupted view of the Sun, free from eclipses and occultation.

 

• Aditya-L1, India's first solar observatory mission, was launched on 2 September 2023 by a PSLV-C57 and was inserted into a halo orbit around L1 in January 2024. Its primary instrument, the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC), studies the solar corona, along with the photosphere, chromosphere, solar wind and coronal mass ejections.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The corona is the outermost layer of the Sun's atmosphere, visible during a total solar eclipse. One of the great unsolved problems of solar physics is why the corona, at over a million degrees, is far hotter than the Sun's visible surface, the photosphere, at about 5,500°C.

 

• Aditya-L1 carries seven payloads, four for remote sensing of the Sun and three for in-situ observation of particles and fields at L1.

 

• The James Webb Space Telescope of NASA is stationed at the L2 point, on the far side of the Earth from the Sun.

 

NOTE

 

• 15,000 km (Option 1) and 1.5 lakh km (Option 2) are far too small; L1 lies well beyond geostationary orbit, which is about 36,000 km.

 

• 15 million km (Option 4) is ten times too large.

question: Which of the following groups consists entirely of ferrous minerals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Iron ore, manganese and chromite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ferrous minerals are metallic minerals that contain iron. The principal ones are iron ore, manganese, chromite, nickel, cobalt and tungsten, and together they form the base of the metallurgical industries. (लौह खनिज — लोहा युक्त धात्विक खनिज)

 

• The classification of minerals:

◦ Metallic minerals

  - Ferrous — iron ore, manganese, chromite, nickel, cobalt

  - Non-ferrous — copper, bauxite, lead, zinc, tin

  - Precious — gold, silver, platinum

◦ Non-metallic minerals — mica, limestone, gypsum, dolomite, potash

◦ Energy (fuel) minerals — coal, petroleum, natural gas, uranium, thorium

 

• India is well endowed with ferrous minerals but deficient in most non-ferrous metallic minerals — copper, zinc, lead and tin are all scarce, and a large part of the requirement is imported.

 

• The four principal varieties of iron ore are magnetite (the finest, with about 70 per cent metallic content and magnetic properties), haematite (the most important industrially, 50-60 per cent), limonite and siderite. Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Jharkhand are the leading producers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manganese is essential in the manufacture of steel — about 10 kg is needed per tonne — and is also used in bleaching powder, insecticides and paints. Odisha is the largest producer.

 

• Copper is prized for being malleable, ductile and a good conductor, and is used in electrical cables, electronics and alloys. Bauxite is the ore from which aluminium is obtained.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Copper and bauxite are non-ferrous, and gold is a precious metal.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Mica, limestone and gypsum are all non-metallic minerals.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Coal, petroleum and natural gas are energy or fuel minerals.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

The National Human Rights Commission of India was established under the ______ Act, 1993.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protection of Human Rights.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It is therefore a statutory body, not a constitutional one. (राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग — मानव अधिकार संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1993)

 

• The Act defines human rights as the rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the individual, guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants and enforceable by courts in India.

 

• Composition: a Chairperson and five full-time members, together with seven deemed members — the chairpersons of the National Commissions for Minorities, SCs, STs, Women, Backward Classes, the Protection of Child Rights, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities. Following the 2019 amendment, the Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice of India or a former judge of the Supreme Court, and the term of office is three years or until the age of 70, whichever is earlier.

 

• Its recommendations are advisory and not binding, and it cannot inquire into a matter after one year of its occurrence. It has limited jurisdiction over the armed forces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bodies are classified as constitutional (Election Commission, CAG, UPSC, Finance Commission, GST Council), statutory (NHRC, NCW, NGT, Lokpal, SEBI, NITI Aayog's predecessor bodies apart) and executive or non-statutory (NITI Aayog, the erstwhile Planning Commission).

 

• Zonal Councils were created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and are therefore statutory bodies. There are five Zonal Councils — Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern — chaired by the Union Home Minister. The North Eastern Council was set up separately by an Act of 1971.

 

NOTE

 

• The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (Option 2): Established the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) to provide free legal aid and to organise Lok Adalats.

 

• The Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952 (Option 3): Provides for the appointment of commissions to inquire into matters of public importance.

 

• The Right to Information Act, 2005 (Option 4): Created the Central and State Information Commissions.

question: Which of the following statements regarding residuary powers of legislation under the Constitution of India is correct?
option_1: Residuary powers are vested in the State Legislatures alone
option_2: Residuary powers are exercised jointly by the Union and the States
option_3: Residuary powers of legislation are vested in Parliament under Article 248
option_4: Residuary powers are exercised by the Supreme Court through judicial interpretation
solution_text:
The correct answer is Residuary powers of legislation are vested in Parliament under Article 248.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 248 provides that Parliament has exclusive power to make any law with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or the State List. This is reinforced by Entry 97 of the Union List, which covers any other matter not mentioned in the other two Lists, including any tax not so mentioned. (अवशिष्ट शक्तियाँ — संसद में निहित, अनुच्छेद 248)

 

• India followed the Canadian model in vesting residuary powers in the Centre, unlike the United States, Australia and Switzerland, where they rest with the States. This is one of the features that makes the Indian Constitution federal in form but unitary in spirit, or quasi-federal.

 

• The Seventh Schedule contains three lists — the Union List (List I), the State List (List II) and the Concurrent List (List III). In case of a conflict on a Concurrent List subject, Union law prevails (Article 254), unless the State law has received the President's assent.

 

• Parliament may legislate on a State List subject in five situations: under Article 249 (Rajya Sabha resolution by a two-thirds majority in the national interest), Article 250 (during a National Emergency), Article 252 (at the request of two or more States), Article 253 (to implement international agreements), and during President's Rule under Article 356.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Under Article 256, the executive power of every State must be exercised so as to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament, and the Union may give such directions to a State as may appear necessary for that purpose. Article 257 extends this to matters of national importance.

 

• Failure of a State to comply with such directions may become a ground for the President to hold, under Article 365, that the government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: In India, unlike the United States, residuary powers rest with the Centre, not the States.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Residuary power is exclusive to Parliament, not shared.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The Supreme Court decides whether a matter falls within residuary power, but the power to legislate belongs to Parliament.

question:
Read the following statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Choose the correct option:

Assertion (A): India observes 23 August every year as National Space Day.

Reason (R): On 23 August 2023, the Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-3 made a successful soft landing near the lunar south pole.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The Government of India declared 23 August as National Space Day, first observed in 2024 with the theme *"Touching Lives while Touching the Moon: India's Space Saga"*. (राष्ट्रीय अंतरिक्ष दिवस — 23 अगस्त)

 

• Reason (R) is true. On 23 August 2023, the Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-3 made a successful soft landing near the lunar south pole, deploying the Pragyan rover.

 

• R correctly explains A. The date was chosen precisely because of that landing. It was not an arbitrary selection: the day commemorates the achievement that made India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first in the world to land near the lunar south pole. R therefore supplies the reason for A, not merely an additional fact.

 

• The landing site has been named Shiv Shakti Point, and the spot where Chandrayaan-2's lander made contact in 2019 is called Tiranga Point.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PSLV-C59, launched in December 2024, successfully placed the European Space Agency's Proba-3 satellites in orbit — the world's first dedicated mission for a precision formation-flying experiment, in which two spacecraft fly as a single structure to create an artificial solar eclipse. It was executed commercially by NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), and marked a notable milestone in international space cooperation.

 

• Other space-related observances: World Space Week, 4-10 October, and National Technology Day, 11 May.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: R is not an unrelated fact; the Chandrayaan-3 landing is the very reason the date was chosen.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question: The National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) is a portal that provides which of the following?
option_1: Real-time data on the institution, pendency and disposal of cases in Indian courts
option_2: A national register of First Information Reports filed at police stations
option_3: A centralised database of prisoners lodged in Indian jails
option_4: Digitised records of rural land holdings across the States
solution_text:
The correct answer is Real-time data on the institution, pendency and disposal of cases in Indian courts.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) is a national repository providing real-time, publicly accessible data on the institution, pendency and disposal of cases in the district and subordinate courts, the High Courts and the Supreme Court. (राष्ट्रीय न्यायिक डेटा ग्रिड)

 

• It was created under the e-Courts Project, a Mission Mode Project under the National e-Governance Plan, monitored by the e-Committee of the Supreme Court of India and implemented with the Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice.

 

• The data can be filtered by state, district, court, case type and age of the case, which makes it a tool for identifying bottlenecks and for judicial administration. The Supreme Court's own data was brought onto the NJDG in 2023.

 

• The World Bank has commended the NJDG as a model of judicial transparency and case management.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, provides for access to the FIR through the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS), a nationwide network linking police stations for the recording, investigation and detection of crime.

 

• Other justice-sector platforms: the Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS), which links the police, courts, prosecution, prisons and forensic laboratories; e-Prisons; and the Tele-Law and Nyaya Bandhu services for legal aid.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: FIR access is provided through the CCTNS platform, not the NJDG.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Prison records are maintained on the e-Prisons platform.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Land records are digitised under the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) and the SVAMITVA scheme.

question:
Which of the following pairs of a Government scheme and its nodal Ministry is/are correctly matched?

1. Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY - Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

2. Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) - Ministry of Rural Development

3. PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal) - Ministry of Women and Child Development

4. Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 4 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pair 1 is correct. Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, which provides health cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year, is implemented by the National Health Authority under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. (आयुष्मान भारत — स्वास्थ्य एवं परिवार कल्याण मंत्रालय)

 

• Pair 2 is correct. Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin) is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development, while PMAY (Urban) falls under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

 

• Pair 3 is incorrect. PM POSHAN, the renamed Mid-Day Meal Scheme, is run by the Ministry of Education (Department of School Education and Literacy), not by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. The latter runs the Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 programme, which is a different scheme.

 

• Pair 4 is correct. Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) is with the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, and SBM (Gramin) with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other scheme-ministry pairings frequently tested:

◦ PM-KISAN, PMFBY, e-NAM — Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare

◦ PM-AASHA — Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, not Consumer Affairs

◦ PMKSY (Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana) — coordinated by the Ministry of Jal Shakti along with Agriculture and Rural Development

◦ RoDTEP — Ministry of Commerce and Industry, though administered through customs

◦ MGNREGA, NRLM (Aajeevika) — Ministry of Rural Development

◦ Jal Jeevan Mission — Ministry of Jal Shakti

◦ PM-SYM and e-Shram — Ministry of Labour and Employment

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1 and 3 are incorrect: Option 1 leaves out Pair 4, which is accurate, and Option 3 includes Pair 3, which is wrong.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: It includes Pair 3, which misassigns the Mid-Day Meal scheme to the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

question:
Fill in the Blank:

The Bidesia folk theatre form, created by the poet and dramatist Bhikhari Thakur, belongs to the state of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bidesia is a popular folk theatre form of Bihar, performed in the Bhojpuri language and created by Bhikhari Thakur (1887-1971), who is often called the "Shakespeare of Bhojpuri". (बिदेसिया — बिहार का लोक रंगमंच)

 

• Its central theme is migration and separation: the sorrow of the wife left behind in the village when her husband migrates to the city in search of work. Through this it dealt with social questions of its time — poverty, migration, caste, dowry and the condition of women.

 

• A distinctive feature of the form is the launda naach, in which male performers play the female roles. Bhikhari Thakur's other well-known works include Gabar Ghichor, Beti Bechwa and Bidhwa Vilap.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major folk theatre forms of India:

◦ Nautanki — Uttar Pradesh

◦ Ramlila and Raslila — Uttar Pradesh, both associated with the epics

◦ Tamasha — Maharashtra

◦ Bhavai — Gujarat

◦ Jatra — West Bengal and Odisha

◦ Yakshagana — Karnataka

◦ Therukoothu — Tamil Nadu

◦ Swang — Haryana

◦ Maach — Madhya Pradesh

◦ Bhand Pather — Jammu and Kashmir

◦ Pandavani — Chhattisgarh, narration from the Mahabharata, made famous by Teejan Bai

 

• The Panthi dance of Chhattisgarh is performed by the Satnami community, the followers of Guru Ghasidas, on his birth anniversary.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Known for the Chhau dance of Seraikela and for Paika and Jhumar.

 

• Odisha (Option 3): Known for Jatra, Prahlad Natak and the classical Odissi.

 

• West Bengal (Option 4): Known for Jatra, Gambhira and Baul singing.

question: On the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) published by Transparency International, countries are scored on a scale in which:
option_1: A score of 0 indicates a very clean country and 100 indicates a highly corrupt one
option_2: A score of 0 indicates a highly corrupt country and 100 indicates a very clean one
option_3: Countries are ranked solely on the basis of their per capita income
option_4: Only developing and least-developed countries are assessed
solution_text:
The correct answer is A score of 0 indicates a highly corrupt country and 100 indicates a very clean one.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) has been published annually by Transparency International since 1995. It scores countries on a scale of 0 to 100, where 0 means highly corrupt and 100 means very clean. (भ्रष्टाचार धारणा सूचकांक — 0 अत्यधिक भ्रष्ट, 100 अत्यंत स्वच्छ)

 

• The index measures perceptions of public sector corruption among business people and country experts, drawing on 13 independent surveys and assessments from institutions such as the World Bank, the World Economic Forum and the Economist Intelligence Unit. It does not measure actual levels of corruption, which cannot be directly observed.

 

• Denmark, Finland, New Zealand, Norway and Singapore have consistently ranked among the cleanest, while conflict-affected states rank lowest.

 

• The CPI 2024 report drew particular attention to the link between corruption and the climate crisis, noting that corruption undermines climate action chiefly by diverting climate funds away from their intended purpose and by allowing undue influence over environmental policy-making.

 

• Transparency International was founded in 1993 and is headquartered at Berlin, Germany.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related indices: the Global Corruption Barometer, also by Transparency International, which surveys citizens' direct experience of bribery; and the Rule of Law Index of the World Justice Project.

 

• In India, the principal anti-corruption institutions are the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), made statutory in 2003, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), and the Lokpal, established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The scale runs the other way — a higher score means a cleaner country.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The CPI measures perceived corruption, not income.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: All countries, developed and developing alike, are assessed; around 180 are covered.

question: What is the principal objective of the Biological Diversity Act, 2002?
option_1: The regulation and control of air pollution from industrial sources
option_2: The protection of ancient monuments and archaeological sites
option_3: The abatement of noise pollution in urban areas
option_4: Conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources
solution_text:
The correct answer is Conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the use of genetic resources.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Biological Diversity Act, 2002, was enacted to give effect in India to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), adopted at the Earth Summit, Rio de Janeiro, 1992. Its three objectives mirror those of the Convention: conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the use of genetic resources. (जैव विविधता अधिनियम, 2002)

 

• The Act establishes a three-tier structure:

◦ the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) at Chennai, a statutory body set up in 2003

◦ State Biodiversity Boards in the States

◦ Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) at the level of local bodies, which maintain People's Biodiversity Registers

 

• It regulates access by foreigners and foreign entities to India's biological resources and associated traditional knowledge, and provides for the notification of Biodiversity Heritage Sites. The Act was amended in 2023 to ease compliance for Indian users and AYUSH practitioners while strengthening benefit sharing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other principal environmental legislation:

◦ Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974

◦ Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981

◦ Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — the umbrella legislation, enacted after the Bhopal gas tragedy

◦ Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980

◦ National Green Tribunal Act, 2010

 

• The objective of India's eco-tourism policy in protected areas is to balance conservation with the livelihoods of local communities, rather than to ban human activity altogether or to maximise commercial profit.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Air pollution is dealt with by the Air Act, 1981.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Monuments are protected by the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Noise is regulated by the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, framed under the Environment (Protection) Act.

question:
Which of the following statements about the jute industry in India is/are correct?

1. West Bengal is the largest producer of raw jute in India.

2. Most of the jute mills are located along the banks of the Hugli river.

3. Jute is popularly known as the "golden fibre".

4. After Partition, India retained most of the jute mills while losing a large part of the jute-growing area.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4 all are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All four statements are correct. (जूट उद्योग)

 

• Statement 1 is correct. West Bengal is the largest producer of raw jute in India, followed by Bihar and Assam. India is among the world's largest producers of raw jute, while Bangladesh leads in the export of jute goods.

 

• Statement 2 is correct. Most jute mills are concentrated in a narrow belt along the banks of the Hugli river in West Bengal, from Naihati to Birlapur. The location is explained by the proximity of the jute-growing areas, cheap water transport, abundant water for processing, coal from the Raniganj fields, cheap labour from Bihar and Odisha, and the port of Kolkata for export.

 

• Statement 3 is correct. Jute is called the "golden fibre" for its golden-brown lustre and its historical value as an export earner.

 

• Statement 4 is correct. At Partition in 1947, India retained most of the mills but lost a large part of the jute-growing tracts to East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) — a mismatch that forced India to expand cultivation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first jute mill in India was set up at Rishra, near Kolkata, in 1855. The Jute Packaging Materials (Compulsory Use in Packing Commodities) Act, 1987, supports demand by requiring the use of jute in packing foodgrains and sugar.

 

• The industry faces competition from synthetic substitutes and from other producing countries. The National Jute Board works on diversification into jute geo-textiles, handicrafts and blended fabrics.

 

• The sugar industry, by contrast, is located close to the cane fields, because sugarcane is a bulky, weight-losing raw material whose sucrose content falls during transportation; it is a seasonal industry, well suited to the cooperative sector, and Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu are among the leading producers.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them omits at least one statement that is factually accurate.

question:
Which of the following statements correctly describe the Namami Gange Programme?

1. It was launched in 2014 as an Integrated Conservation Mission for the rejuvenation of the river Ganga.

2. It is implemented by the National Mission for Clean Ganga under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

3. It is financed entirely by grants from the World Bank.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Namami Gange Programme was approved in 2014 as an Integrated Conservation Mission, with the twin objectives of abatement of pollution and conservation and rejuvenation of the river Ganga. (नमामि गंगे कार्यक्रम, 2014)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. It is implemented by the National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG), which functions under the Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti. The NMCG was given statutory backing by an order under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, and the apex body is the National Ganga Council, chaired by the Prime Minister.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect. The programme is a Central Sector Scheme financed by the Government of India. The World Bank has supported some components through the National Ganga River Basin Project, but the programme is not financed entirely by World Bank grants.

 

• Its main pillars are sewerage treatment infrastructure, river-front development, river-surface cleaning, afforestation, industrial effluent monitoring, biodiversity conservation, public awareness and Ganga Gram.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ganga was declared the National River of India in 2008. The earlier Ganga Action Plan was launched in 1985.

 

• The Dolphin — the Gangetic river dolphin — is the National Aquatic Animal of India, and Project Dolphin was announced to protect it.

 

• The MISHTI scheme — Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes — announced in the Union Budget 2023-24, is designed to increase mangrove cover and enhance coastal livelihoods, and is financed through a convergence of MGNREGS, CAMPA and other funds. It is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, not the Ministry of Rural Development.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because each of them includes Statement 3, which wrongly attributes the entire financing of the programme to the World Bank.

question:
Which of the following statements about India's entries on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity are correct?

1. Kutiyattam, the Sanskrit theatre of Kerala, was among the earliest Indian entries on the list.

2. Durga Puja in Kolkata was inscribed on the list in 2021.

3. Yoga was inscribed on the list in 2016.
solution_text:
The correct answer is All 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct. (यूनेस्को अमूर्त सांस्कृतिक विरासत — भारत)

 

• Statement 1 is correct. Kutiyattam, the Sanskrit theatre of Kerala, was recognised by UNESCO in 2001 and formally inscribed in 2008. It was India's first entry, and is among the oldest living theatre traditions in the world.

 

• Statement 2 is correct. Durga Puja in Kolkata was inscribed in 2021, the first festival from Asia to receive the honour.

 

• Statement 3 is correct. Yoga was inscribed in 2016. The International Day of Yoga is observed on 21 June, following a resolution of the UN General Assembly in 2014.

 

• India's other entries include the Vedic chanting tradition, Ramlila, Ramman of Uttarakhand, Chhau dance, Kalbelia folk songs and dances of Rajasthan, Mudiyettu of Kerala, Buddhist chanting of Ladakh, Sankirtana of Manipur, the brass and copper craft of Punjab (Thatheras), Nawrouz, Yoga, the Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja and Garba of Gujarat (2023).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kalbelia dance of Rajasthan was inscribed in 2010. It is performed by the Kalbelia snake-charmer community; the dancers' swirling black skirts and sinuous movements imitate the movements of serpents. Being an oral, nomadic tradition, its songs and dances have been passed on largely without written documentation.

 

• The distinction to remember: the World Heritage List covers tangible sites — monuments and natural areas — while the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity covers living traditions, such as performing arts, rituals, festivals and craftsmanship.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because each of them omits at least one statement that is factually accurate.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and cannot be dissolved.

2. One-third of the members of the Rajya Sabha retire every second year.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Rajya Sabha is a continuing or permanent chamber and is not subject to dissolution. This is provided by Article 83(1). (राज्यसभा — स्थायी सदन, विघटन नहीं)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. One-third of its members retire every second year, and elections are held to fill those seats. Each member holds office for a term of six years.

 

• The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 — 238 representatives of the States and Union Territories, elected indirectly, and 12 nominated by the President from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

 

• Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies through proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. Seats are allotted to States in the Fourth Schedule, roughly in proportion to population, so representation is not equal for all States — unlike the United States Senate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Special powers of the Rajya Sabha: it alone may pass a resolution under Article 249 enabling Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in the national interest, and under Article 312 to create a new All-India Service — each requiring a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

 

• A Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha, which may only make recommendations within 14 days. Note the distinction that every Money Bill is a Financial Bill, but every Financial Bill is not a Money Bill — a Money Bill is confined to the matters listed in Article 110.

 

• The Vice-President of India is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and is not a member of the House.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.
